# Disagreement Log — T12_001 (Testament of Reuben)
**Chapter:** T12_001 | **Verses:** 6 chapters (~25 sections)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 1:5 | Verb for Reuben's sin | "I was poured-out" (literal ekcheo) | "I was poured out, and defiled" (combined) | "gave yourself to sexual sin" (functional) | "in which I was poured out, and defiled" — LOGOS captures both verbs |
| 2 | 2:3–9 | Structure of seven spirits | Numbered list with dash format | Flowing enumeration in paragraph | Narrative with brief labels | Enumerated with paragraph flow; LOGOS structure adopted |
| 3 | 3:1 | "Watchers" episode placement | Included in chapter 2 | Placed as opening of chapter 3 | Summarized briefly in transition | Follows LOGOS chapter division; Watchers named explicitly |
| 4 | 4:4–5 | Location detail (Eder/Bethlehem) | Preserved "Eder, near Ephrath in Bethlehem" | Preserved with slight expansion | Omitted for narrative flow | EMET/LOGOS location detail retained; PNEUMA omission rejected |
| 5 | 5:3 | "Constant meetings" clause | "constant-meetings" (hyphenated) | "constant meetings, even though the ungodly deed be not wrought" | "even when nothing happens, the constant proximity is a disease" | LOGOS phrasing adopted as clearest formal rendering |
| 6 | 6:3 | "princes" vs "rulers" | "rulers among the people" | "princes among the people" | "lords over the people" | "princes among the people" — LOGOS adopted; PNEUMA "lords" rejected as dominance-flavored |

---
*SOPHIA notes: The Testament of Reuben presents a consistent moralizing framework. PNEUMA usefully restructures the seven-spirits list as a numbered sequence but loses manuscript verse markers. EMET's hyphenation is preserved internally but softened in the consensus. All three agree on the core confession narrative of Bilhah.*
